To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the vacuum fluctuations are important in the description of the hard processes in QED; (2) the vacuum fluctuations can be taken into account in a systematic way by introducing a new type of the parton cross sections; and (3) the vacuum fluctuations do not lead to any additional divergences in the cross sections.
the vacuum fluctuations are important for hard processes and cannot be neglected.
the impulse approximation in QED and in QCD is not valid in the presence of soft photons and soft gluons, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of factorizing QCD processes.
the question of the validity of the impulse approximation in QED and in QCD in the presence of the vacuum fluctuations.
the question of how the idea of factorizability of hard processes can be generalized to include vacuum fluctuations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factorization idea is not applicable in the presence of soft gluon effects, i.e., the idea of factorizing hard processes in QED and QCD cannot be extended to higher twist effects.
vacuum fluctuations are important in QCD, and that the impulse approximation is not applicable in general, even in the leading order.
the vacuum fluctuations do not spoil the factorization in QCD, but the factorization is not the same as that in the free theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the factorization is not a general property of QCD and it is not possible to define parton cross sections in a gauge invariant manner in the presence of infrared divergences.
the vacuum fluctuations do not allow a factorization in terms of partonic distributions and hard cross sections.
the impulse approximation in QED is valid to all orders of perturbation theory and the impulse approximation in quantum chromodynamics is valid only in the leading order.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vacuum fluctuations are a source of nontrivial correlations in QCD and that these correlations are not taken into account in the impulse approximation.
the vacuum fluctuations are not a small effect and should be taken into account in any realistic description of hard processes in QED and QCD.
the factorization of hard processes in QED is a special case of a more general phenomenon, namely the factorization of the scattering matrix.
